# Bench

> A custody kernel for agent work — not an agent. Bench gives an unreliable worker (the "intern") five verbs (READ, WRITE, EXEC, TEST, WAIT), frames each step under a clock and quotas, seals a content-hashed snapshot after every step, and lets only the owner crown work into the main tree. Linux only. No model in the tree. License: MIT OR Apache-2.0.

Facts an agent needs:
- You emit one op per line: `READ fs <path>`, `WRITE fs <hold/…|proposed/…> <one line>`, `EXEC tools/<name>.py <args>`, `TEST PURE|SCALAR tests/rom/<t>.py`, `WAIT <ms>`. No sixth verb.
- A refusal prints `rule=<id> fix: <hint>`. Act on the fix; do not retry the same line. All ids: {{ '/api/rules.json' | absolute_url }}
- A parse fault refuses the whole script before any frame. A run-time refusal stops the run at that step (the step is snapshotted with its rule).
- Budgets: N=8 frames, T_tool=5 s per worker, T_frame=200 ms, hold/ growth 64 KiB and 256 entries per session, 4096 bytes of output per step.
- Repository work: run `make env && make ledger-test`, report the summary (not the log), read HANDOFF.md, one concern per commit, spec/ meaning is frozen.
- Never put tokens or sessions/ contents in a chat, commit or log.
